title: Acute:chronic workload ratio and load management for team sports: a multilevel meta-analysis
claims: This PROSPERO-registered (CRD420245127618) systematic review and multilevel meta-analysis covered team-sport athletes; 41 studies met inclusion criteria and 16 studies involving 797 athletes were included in the meta-analysis.
Elevated ACWR showed a small-to-moderate association with higher injury risk, Hedges' g = 0.35 (95% CI 0.16–0.54), with substantial heterogeneity (I² = 95.8%).
Associations were stronger for contact and non-contact injuries, whereas effects were not significant for time-loss injuries or other moderators.

The conclusion is that current evidence does not support ACWR as a stand-alone causal or predictive model; it should be interpreted as a contextual monitoring indicator within individualized, multi-marker load-management systems.

verification.note: 2026-11-26 直取 Frontiers 全文；核对纳入研究数、797 人、g=0.35、CI、I²=95.8%、time-loss 不显著与结论段。研究对象为团队项目运动员，不是路跑人群。
